title: TS parity replayer: 10k hands, zero divergence
description:
## Objective
A TS harness that replays Python-recorded traces into the TS engine and asserts every intermediate legal-action set, trick winner, and score matches — the port acceptance gate.

## Behavioral context
After M1 the TS engine passes its own tests but has no proof of oracle fidelity. After this leaf, >= 10,000 recorded hands replay with zero divergence, and a divergence prints the exact hand/step context (PRD section 7.2).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/engine/test/parity/replay.ts`: stream a .jsonl trace, for each hand construct GameState from the recorded deal (bypassing rng), feed recorded actions via applyAction, and assert at every step: TS legal sets equal recorded legal sets, trick winners match, hand deltas and redeals match. Plus `parity.spec.ts` running a committed 200-hand fixture in CI-less `pnpm test`, and a script `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine parity` for the full 10k run against generated traces.

## Non-goals
No attempt at RNG stream equivalence (explicitly rejected by the PRD); no fixing of engine bugs here beyond filing them — divergences are engine defects to fix under M1 leaves unless the trace is wrong.

## Concrete locations
Consumes trace schema from trace_500.py (related leaf) and the GameState API from packages/engine/src/state.ts; needs a deal-injection entry (`initHandFromDeal(hands, middle, first)`) — add it to state.ts as a test-only export. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Card encoding is identity (decided in the cards leaf) so traces need no mapping layer; the committed fixture (200 hands, auction-weighted seed) keeps `pnpm test` fast while the 10k gate runs on demand; divergence output includes hand index, phase, seat, expected vs actual as JSON.

## Compatibility constraints
The fixture file lives under packages/engine/test/parity/fixtures/ and is regenerated only by the documented trace_500.py command line recorded in a README next to it.

## Ordered steps
1. Add initHandFromDeal test export to state.ts.
2. Implement the streaming replayer with per-step assertions.
3. Generate and commit the 200-hand fixture (command recorded).
4. Wire parity.spec.ts into the package test script; add the `parity` script for full runs.
5. Generate 10k+ hands (mixed + auction-weighted traces), run to zero divergence, and record the command + result in the issue notes on close.

## Dependencies
Blocked by: the section-7.1 suite leaf (green engine) and the Python trace emitter leaf. Consumers: M5 client work is gated on this epic per the PRD dependency shape.

## Edge cases
Redeal-only hands (no play section); slam hands where the recorded keeps came from 16 cards; joker-led records must carry the named suit; trace records with the "illegal bid treated as pass" oracle branch must replay without the TS legalBids offering them.

## Plan-gap guidance
On any divergence where the TS engine, the Python oracle, and 500-house-rules.md cannot be reconciled by fixing an obvious port bug, record `PLAN-GAP` with the minimal diverging trace snippet and stop; do not adjust the trace or loosen an assertion.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: The committed 200-hand fixture replays with zero divergence in the normal test run.
- AC-2: A full run of >= 10,000 hands (mixed and auction-weighted traces) reports zero divergence.
- AC-3: An intentionally corrupted trace line fails with a diagnostic naming hand index, phase, and expected vs actual.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- parity`.
- AC-2: Run `python trace_500.py --seed 7 --hands 10000 > /tmp/t.jsonl && pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine parity /tmp/t.jsonl`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- parity` (includes the corruption unit case).

## Targeted tests
Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- test/parity/parity.spec.ts` (committed 200-hand fixture). Full-scale check: `python trace_500.py --seed 7 --hands 10000 > /tmp/t.jsonl && pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine parity /tmp/t.jsonl`.

CodeGraph unavailable for this repo (no .codegraph index; handshake query failed as expected). All file/symbol evidence gathered via Read and grep of five_hundred.py (line refs cited) and 500-house-rules.md. All TS paths are greenfield per PRD section 2 layout.

## Full-scale parity runs (recorded on close, packet step 5)
All commands from repo root; every run reported zero divergence.

- AC-2 (exact command): 'uv run python trace_500.py --seed 7 --hands 10000 > /tmp/t.jsonl && pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine parity /tmp/t.jsonl' -> parity OK: zero divergence over 10000 hands (103576 deals, 93576 redeals, 429399 auction actions, 10000 exchanges, 396540 plays, 100000 tricks, 10000 hand results, 1153091 trace lines)
- mixed: '--seed 11 --hands 10000 --policies mixed' -> zero divergence (30378 deals, 20378 redeals, 145727 auction actions, 399420 plays, 100000 tricks)
- auction-weighted: '--seed 13 --hands 10000 --auction-only' -> zero divergence (10000 deals, 41518 auction actions)
- stress (NULLA/DNULLA/slam heavy): '--seed 17 --hands 10000 --policies stress' -> zero divergence (37995 deals, 27995 redeals, 167302 auction actions, 352130 plays, 100000 tricks)

Total: 40,000 hands replayed, zero divergence. AC-1/AC-3: 'pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- parity' -> 158/158 tests pass incl. parity.spec.ts (committed 200-hand stress fixture, seed 19, regeneration command in test/parity/fixtures/README.md; 3 corruption cases produce hand/phase/expected-vs-actual diagnostics).

Implementation notes: tsx was an undeclared hoisted bin; declared as engine devDependency and lockfile importer entry added (verified with pnpm install --lockfile-only). Sandbox-only caveat: the tsx CLI wrapper opens an IPC unix socket, blocked in the agent sandbox, so the pnpm parity script was verified there via the identical loader path 'node --import tsx/dist/loader.mjs test/parity/cli.ts'; outside the sandbox the script runs as written.

title: Python trace mode: JSON-lines emitter for parity
description:
## Objective
A Python script that plays K seeded hands with deterministic policies and emits a JSON-lines trace of deals, auction actions, legal-play sets, trick winners, and hand scores.

## Behavioral context
No trace capability exists today; five_hundred.py only prints stats. After this leaf, `python trace_500.py --seed 1 --hands 1000 > traces.jsonl` produces a stable, replayable record for the TS engine (PRD section 7.2).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
New `trace_500.py` at repo root importing five_hundred (do not modify the oracle beyond zero-risk hooks): run play_one_hand-equivalent flow with instrumented policies, emitting one JSON object per event: deal (hands+middle), each auction action with the legal set implied, exchange keeps/slam/giveCard, each play with the legal_plays set at that point, joker named suits, trick winners, and the HandResult. Include seed, hand index, and first seat in every record. Also add `test_trace_500.py` (stdlib unittest, no pytest dependency): an in-process smoke test that traces 5 hands and asserts JSON validity, v1 schema fields, and byte-determinism across two runs.

## Non-goals
No TS code; no changes to oracle game logic; no multi-process performance work.

## Concrete locations
Wraps five_hundred.py symbols: deal (513), run_auction (384) — needs an instrumented copy or callback since the loop is closed; _exchange_middle (430) and play_hand (465) likewise; HeuristicPolicy (241) as the deterministic policy with random.Random(seed). Decision below resolves the closed-loop problem. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
trace_500.py re-implements the run_auction/play_hand driver loops verbatim (copy the ~60 lines) with emit() calls inserted, importing all primitives (legal_plays, card_power, effective_suit, scoring via the same arithmetic) from five_hundred — duplicating only the two driver loops keeps the oracle file untouched while guaranteeing identical logic paths; policies are 4x HeuristicPolicy plus a mixed Heuristic/Random config flag; trace schema version field `v: 1`; auction records include ladder_pos before the action so the TS side can check legalBids.

## Compatibility constraints
Python 3.10+ stdlib only (json, argparse, random); output stable across runs given the same seed and args; hands weighted toward auctions via a --auction-only mode flag for the PRD section 9 auction-heavy traces.

## Ordered steps
1. Write the emit schema (documented at the top of trace_500.py).
2. Copy and instrument the auction driver; emit action + pre-action ladder_pos + may_indicate.
3. Copy and instrument exchange + play drivers; emit legal sets, plays, named joker suits, trick winners.
4. Emit HandResult per hand; support --seed, --hands, --policies, --auction-only.
5. Spot-verify: for one seed, assert final printed stats match a direct simulate_hands run.
6. Add the `test_trace_500.py` stdlib-unittest smoke test.

## Dependencies
No issue dependency — Python-side work, independent of the TS engine. Related: the TS replayer leaf consumes this schema. Consumers: tests/parity in packages/engine.

## Edge cases
Redeals must be emitted (they are auction outcomes to verify); slam hands emit the 16-card keeps context; JSON must encode card ints as-is (identity mapping decided in the cards leaf); large K must stream, not accumulate in memory.

## Plan-gap guidance
If instrumenting requires changing oracle behavior (not just copying loops), record `PLAN-GAP` with the exact function and stop — the oracle must remain the untouched reference.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: `python trace_500.py --seed 1 --hands 50` emits valid JSON-lines with the documented v1 schema fields.
- AC-2: Two runs with identical args produce byte-identical output.
- AC-3: A run includes at least one redeal, one nulla, one slam, and one dnulla record across a documented seed/hands combination recorded in the script header.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `python trace_500.py --seed 1 --hands 50 | python -c "import json,sys; [json.loads(l) for l in sys.stdin]; print(\"OK\")"`.
- AC-2: Run `python trace_500.py --seed 1 --hands 50 | sha256sum` twice and compare.
- AC-3: Run `python trace_500.py --seed 1 --hands 2000 | grep -c -e DNULLA -e NULLA` and the documented check from the script header.

## Targeted tests
Run `python -m unittest -v test_trace_500` — `test_trace_500.py` is a new stdlib-unittest smoke file added by this leaf (traces 5 hands in-process; asserts every emitted line parses as JSON with the v1 schema fields and that two identical runs are byte-identical). No pytest suite exists in this repo. Also run `python -m py_compile trace_500.py` and the AC checks above.

description:
## Objective
The complete PRD section 7.1 Vitest suite: every _self_test assertion plus the enumerated new cases, acting as the M1 exit gate.

## Behavioral context
Individual engine leaves carry local tests; this leaf consolidates the milestone acceptance list so M1 has one green gate before parity work begins.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/engine/test/rules.spec.ts` (plus per-area spec files as needed) covering, from PRD section 7.1: ladder ordering incl. nulla/dnulla placements; avondale values; bower following; joker-blocks-sluffing; joker silent-suit-assumption; auction quiet-count endings; redeal; double-nulla pass-through exchange; slam 16-to-10 flow; scoring for every contract class incl. defender points on lose-all; out-the-back; both-cross-500 tiebreak.

## Non-goals
No parity harness (M2), no bot tests, no restructuring of engine code beyond what failures force.

## Concrete locations
Oracle asserts to port verbatim: _self_test (five_hundred.py 652-673). Each PRD 7.1 item maps to the engine modules from the prior five leaves. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
This suite tests through the public GameState API wherever possible (not internals) so it survives refactors and doubles as API documentation; one `it` per PRD 7.1 bullet minimum, named after the rule.

## Compatibility constraints
Suite must run in plain `vitest run` with no network or worker threads.

## Ordered steps
1. Port the 10 _self_test assertions.
2. Add the PRD 7.1 enumerated cases not already covered by leaf-local tests, through the public API.
3. Cross-link: delete or dedupe overlapping leaf-local tests where this suite supersedes them.
4. Ensure `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test` is green.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the GameState assembly leaf. Consumers: parity replayer builds on a green M1; epic M1 closes on this leaf.

## Edge cases
The suite itself must cover the edge list from PRD 7.1 — treat each bullet as mandatory; a skipped or todo-marked test leaves this leaf unfinished.

## Plan-gap guidance
Any ported assertion that fails against the TS engine indicates port drift: fix the engine to match the oracle. If the oracle assertion itself contradicts 500-house-rules.md, record `PLAN-GAP` quoting both sources and stop.

title: Engine: GameState assembly — applyAction, legalActions, redactedView, serialization
description:
## Objective
One pure state machine tying deal, auction, exchange, play, and scoring into GameState + applyAction with legalActions(state, seat), redactedView(state, seat), and JSON serialization.

## Behavioral context
This is the API the server, bots, parity replayer, and client types all consume (PRD section 3.6). After this leaf a complete multi-hand game is drivable purely through actions, and per-seat views never contain hidden cards.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/engine/src/state.ts`: phase union `dealing | auction | middleExchange | slamDecision | partnerCard | play | handScored | gameOver`; Action union (bid, discardKeeps, declareSlam, declineSlam, giveCard, playCard, nextHand); applyAction validating actor/turn/phase; legalActions enumerating exact legal moves; redactedView hiding other hands, the middle, and discards while exposing counts, contract, trick, scores, sat-out seats; serialize/deserialize round-trip; redeal handling (auto redeal on dead auction, dealer rotation).

## Non-goals
No networking, no policy logic, no view formatting beyond data.

## Concrete locations
Composes the four prior engine leaves; oracle cross-checks: play_one_hand redeal loop (five_hundred.py 521-531), play_game rotation (537-555). New file packages/engine/src/state.ts plus index.ts exports. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Reducer style `applyAction(state, action) -> state` returning a Result with a typed error (never throwing) so the server can map invalid commands to protocol errors; explicit declineSlam action so the NUM exchange cannot stall ambiguously; nextHand requires ready-up from every human seat (server decides which seats are human via an actor mask parameter kept out of the engine — engine just exposes handScored until nextHand is applied by the driver); dealing phase is internal: applying nextHand deals via the injected rng and enters auction.

## Compatibility constraints
State and views are pure JSON (no classes/Maps) so structured-clone, WS transport, and worker threads all work; API shape is frozen here — protocol and bots leaves import these types.

## Ordered steps
1. Define GameState, phase union, Action union, and typed errors.
2. Wire deal -> auction -> exchange (with slam sub-phases) -> play -> handScored -> gameOver | next deal, including auto-redeal.
3. Implement legalActions per phase/seat.
4. Implement redactedView with card-count-only opponents and hidden middle/discards.
5. Implement serialize/deserialize with a version field.
6. Tests: scripted full games per contract class; redaction property test (no hidden card ids appear in any view); serialize round-trip mid-game.

## Dependencies
Blocked by: rng/deal, auction, exchange, and trick/scoring leaves. Consumers: packages/protocol (view types), packages/bots (Policy calls), apps/server (authoritative loop), parity replayer.

## Edge cases
Action by a non-active (sat-out) seat rejected; action out of turn rejected; playCard with jokerSuit when not leading the joker rejected; redeal preserves game scores and rotates the dealer; gameOver freezes all actions except nothing (terminal).

## Plan-gap guidance
If any phase transition cannot be expressed without policy knowledge leaking into the engine (e.g. who confirms nextHand), record `PLAN-GAP` describing the coupling instead of importing bot/server concepts into packages/engine.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: A scripted full game (auction through gameOver) runs through applyAction only, for each of NUM, slam, nulla, and dnulla contracts.
- AC-2: For every reachable state in the scripted games, redactedView(seat) contains no card id from another hand, the middle, or discards.
- AC-3: serialize/deserialize round-trips mid-auction, mid-exchange, and mid-trick states with deep equality.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- state`.
- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- redaction`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- state`.

## Targeted tests
Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- test/state.spec.ts` (spec added by this leaf under `packages/engine/test/`).

title: Engine: trick play loop and hand/game scoring
description:
## Objective
The 10-trick play loop over active seats with joker lead handling, plus hand scoring (all contract classes) and game scoring with the +500/-500 termination and both-cross tiebreak.

## Behavioral context
After this leaf a full hand can be played action-by-action to a HandResult, and hand deltas accumulate to a game result exactly as play_game does.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/engine/src/play.ts`: trick state (leader, ledSuit, plays), playCard action with optional jokerSuit (required exactly when leading the joker and trump is null), winner = max cardPower, seat rotation over activeSeats only; `packages/engine/src/scoring.ts`: HandResult port and game accumulation.

## Non-goals
No policy decisions; no serialization/redaction (assembly leaf).

## Concrete locations
Oracle: play_hand trick loop (five_hundred.py 472-510) — order rotation 473-474, joker-led suit naming 483-487, winner 489-491; scoring branches 496-508 (lose-all: made = declTricks == 0, defenders 10 * declTricks; slam: made = declTricks == 10, delta +/-(value+250), defenders 10 * defTricks; NUM: made = declTricks >= level); game loop play_game (537-555) — declarer side checked first when both cross 500 in one hand (546-553), first rotates (first+1)%4, documented assumption: declarer leads trick 1 (line 471 leader = declarer). Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
jokerSuit is a field on the playCard action rather than a separate phase — legalActions will enumerate playCard(JOKER, suit) variants when leading under null trump; a played (non-led) joker silently assumes the led suit via effectiveSuit; trick history (all 10 tricks with winners) is retained on the state for the last-trick UI peek and parity assertions.

## Compatibility constraints
Scoring numbers must match the rules doc table and oracle exactly; state JSON-plain.

## Ordered steps
1. Implement trick state + playCard validation via legalPlays over the acting seat.
2. Implement joker lead suit naming and silent assumption.
3. Implement winner resolution and leader rotation among activeSeats.
4. Port HandResult scoring branches.
5. Implement game score accumulation with termination and tiebreak ordering.
6. Tests: sit-out rotation (3 active seats), joker led/followed, each scoring branch, out-the-back, both-cross tiebreak.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the tricks/legality leaf and the exchange leaf. Consumers: state assembly, sim harness, Hard-bot rollouts (which replay this loop).

## Edge cases
Nulla with 3 active players still plays 10 tricks; defender points on lose-all use tricks forced onto the bidding side; slam failure subtracts value+250 even when 9 tricks were taken; a side can win on defender points; both sides crossing +500 in one hand resolves for the declarer side first; a side at exactly -500 goes out the back.

## Plan-gap guidance
The oracle documents its assumptions block (five_hundred.py 26-30) — declarer leads first, declarer-side-first tiebreak. These are adopted as product decisions. If any other unstated tie appears (e.g. both sides at -500 in one hand), record `PLAN-GAP` with the state rather than inventing a rule.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: Scoring unit cases match the oracle for: made/set NUM, nulla made/set with defender points = 10 per declarer trick, dnulla, slam made (+value+250) and failed (-(value+250)).
- AC-2: A game where both sides cross +500 in the same hand is won by the declarer side.
- AC-3: With a sat-out partner, rotation covers exactly 3 seats and all 10 tricks resolve with a winner.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- scoring`.
- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- scoring`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- play`.

## Targeted tests
Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- test/play.spec.ts test/scoring.spec.ts` (specs added by this leaf under `packages/engine/test/`).

title: Engine: middle exchange, slam, and double-nulla pass-through
description:
## Objective
Action-driven exchange phase: declarer 15-card pickup and 5 discards, optional slam declaration with partner best-card surrender (16 keep 10), nulla partner sit-out, and double-nulla 5-card pass-through to partner.

## Behavioral context
Python does this in one closed function (_exchange_middle); the web game needs it as discrete actions (declareSlam, giveCard, discardKeeps) so humans can act at each step. After this leaf every contract class reaches the play phase with 10-card hands and the correct active-seat set.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/engine/src/exchange.ts`: ExchangeState covering: NUM contract — declarer holds hand+middle (15), may declareSlam (then partner must giveCard, declarer holds 16, partner becomes inactive) then discardKeeps to 10; NULLA — declarer 15 keep 10, partner inactive; DNULLA — declarer 15 keep 10, the exact 5 discards travel to partner who then holds 15 and keeps 10, all four seats stay active. Produces {activeSeats, slam, discards}.

## Non-goals
No UI, no bot keep heuristics, no trick play.

## Concrete locations
Oracle: _exchange_middle (five_hundred.py 430-462) — partner = (declarer+2)%4; DNULLA branch 435-443 (passed = cards not kept); NULLA branch 444-448; slam branch 450-460 (consider_slam then give_best_card, hands[partner].remove(best), cards+[best]); invariant assert line 461. Rules doc sections "The middle (kitty)" and "Slamming". Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Slam is offered exactly once, while the declarer holds the 15 and before discardKeeps, numbered contracts only (no slam on nulla/dnulla per rules doc); the slam decision is its own action so the UI confirm step maps 1:1; discardKeeps takes the kept-card list and validates it is exactly 10 cards drawn from the held set; sit-out seats are represented in activeSeats, not by emptying hands.

## Compatibility constraints
States must serialize to JSON; the discards list stays hidden from redacted views (later leaf) but must be stored for slam extra-card return per rules doc.

## Ordered steps
1. Define ExchangeState and entry from an auction result.
2. Implement discardKeeps with 10-card validation for each contract class.
3. Implement declareSlam and giveCard transitions.
4. Implement DNULLA pass-through carrying the exact 5 discards.
5. Tests per contract class: hand sizes, activeSeats, slam 16-to-10, pass-through card identity.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the auction leaf (contract/declarer types). Consumers: game-state assembly, exchange UI leaves, Hard-bot keeps evaluation.

## Edge cases
Keeping cards not held or keeping 9/11 cards must be rejected with no state change; declarer keeping all 5 original middle cards is legal; slam giveCard must come from the partner hand; after slam the partner has 9 cards and sits out; DNULLA partner must receive exactly the 5 discards, not a reshuffle.

## Plan-gap guidance
The rules doc says the slam extra card is discarded "back into the middle discards" — the oracle folds it into choose_keeps from 16. If any downstream consumer needs the two discard piles distinguished, record `PLAN-GAP` instead of inventing a distinction.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: For each contract class (NUM, NUM+slam, NULLA, DNULLA) the exchange ends with every active seat holding exactly 10 cards and the correct activeSeats set.
- AC-2: DNULLA partner pickup contains exactly the 5 cards the declarer discarded.
- AC-3: Invalid keeps (wrong count or cards not held) are rejected and state is unchanged.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- exchange`.
- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- exchange`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- exchange`.

## Targeted tests
Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- test/exchange.spec.ts` (spec added by this leaf under `packages/engine/test/`).

title: Engine: seeded RNG and deal
description:
## Objective
An injectable seeded RNG plus the deal function producing 4 sorted 10-card hands and a 5-card middle.

## Behavioral context
The engine must be deterministic under a seed (PRD section 2); after this leaf, dealing with the same seed always yields the same hands, and no engine code calls Math.random or Date.now.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/engine/src/rng.ts`: an `Rng` interface (`random(): number`, `int(n): number`, `shuffle(arr): void`) with a mulberry32-based implementation `makeRng(seed: number)`. `packages/engine/src/deal.ts`: port of deal (five_hundred.py lines 513-518) — shuffle a copy of DECK, hands = 4 sorted slices of 10, middle = last 5.

## Non-goals
No attempt to reproduce the CPython Mersenne-Twister stream — parity replays recorded deals instead (PRD section 7.2).

## Concrete locations
Oracle: deal (five_hundred.py 513-518), DECK (72). New files as above. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
mulberry32 PRNG (32-bit seed) with in-place Fisher-Yates shuffle using `int(n)`; the Rng interface is the only randomness entry point for engine and bots, so Hard-bot rollouts and tests can inject their own.

## Compatibility constraints
Pure TS, no runtime deps; identical results in Node and browsers (no BigInt, only >>> arithmetic).

## Ordered steps
1. Implement makeRng with random/int/shuffle.
2. Implement deal(rng) returning {hands, middle} with sorted hands.
3. Tests: fixed seed snapshot; all 45 cards partitioned exactly once; repeat-call determinism.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the cards/ladder leaf (DECK). Consumers: game state assembly, bots sim harness, Hard-bot world sampling.

## Edge cases
shuffle of empty/1-length arrays; int(n) must be uniform over [0,n) and never return n; two makeRng(seed) instances must not share state.

## Plan-gap guidance
None expected — if determinism across platforms proves impossible with the chosen PRNG, record `PLAN-GAP` with a failing cross-run diff rather than switching algorithms silently.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: deal(makeRng(42)) twice produces identical hands and middle (snapshot test).
- AC-2: Every deal partitions all 45 distinct cards into 4x10 sorted hands + 5 middle.
- AC-3: `grep -rn "Math.random\|Date.now" packages/engine/src` returns nothing.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- deal`.
- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- deal`.
- AC-3: Run `grep -rn "Math.random\|Date.now" packages/engine/src || echo CLEAN` and expect CLEAN.

## Targeted tests
Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- test/deal.spec.ts` (spec added by this leaf under `packages/engine/test/`; covers makeRng determinism and the deal port).

title: Engine: auction state machine
description:
## Objective
An incremental, action-driven auction: bids, one-per-player indications, quiet-count termination, and redeal detection matching run_auction.

## Behavioral context
The Python run_auction is a closed loop over policies; the web game needs the same rules as a step-per-action state machine so humans can act. After this leaf, feeding any action sequence produces the same contract/declarer/indications/redeal outcome the oracle would.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/engine/src/auction.ts`: AuctionState {ladderPos, declarer, indications, indicated[4], consecutiveQuiet, turn}; `applyAuctionAction(state, seat, bid)`; `legalBids(state, seat)` listing strictly-higher ladder bids, IND (only while declarer is null and seat has not indicated), and PASS; terminal results: contract won (3 quiet after a winning bid) or redeal (4 quiet with no winner).

## Non-goals
No bot bidding logic; no UI concerns; exchange handled in a separate leaf.

## Concrete locations
Oracle: run_auction + AuctionResult (five_hundred.py 377-411): note consecutive_quiet resets on winning bids AND on indications (line 404), illegal/low bids count as passes (line 400), thresholds >=3 with declarer and >=4 without. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Server-facing legalBids never offers an out-of-turn or below-ladder bid, so the "illegal bid counted as pass" branch exists only for parity replay tolerance; state is immutable (each apply returns a new state) to match the whole-engine reducer style; turn advances (seat+1)%4 from the `first` seat.

## Compatibility constraints
Action/state shapes will be serialized into protocol messages — keep them JSON-plain.

## Ordered steps
1. Define AuctionState + init(first).
2. Implement legalBids per the ladder and indication rules.
3. Implement applyAuctionAction with quiet-count bookkeeping identical to lines 391-411.
4. Tests: contract after 3 passes; redeal on 4 passes; redeal on indications-only; indication keeps auction alive; second indication by same player counts as pass; declarer overtaken by later higher bid.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the cards/ladder leaf (LADDER). Consumers: game-state assembly, auction UI, parity replayer (auction traces are weighted per PRD section 9).

## Edge cases
Indication after a winning bid exists is illegal (may_indicate requires declarer null); a player may indicate then later win the auction; ladderPos at top of ladder leaves only PASS; exactly-3-quiet boundary immediately after a bid.

## Plan-gap guidance
PRD section 3.2 says auction ends when 3 consecutive non-bids follow a winning bid, and Python treats an indication as resetting quiet even though indications are only legal before a winning bid — if replayed traces expose any other divergence in quiet counting, record `PLAN-GAP` with the trace rather than patching to fit.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: Bid 7S then three passes yields contract 7S with correct declarer; four passes from the start yields redeal.
- AC-2: An auction of only indications yields redeal, and each seat can indicate at most once.
- AC-3: legalBids never contains a bid at or below ladderPos, and contains IND only when legal.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- auction`.
- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- auction`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- auction`.

## Targeted tests
Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/engine test -- test/auction.spec.ts` (spec added by this leaf under `packages/engine/test/`).

title: Engine: effective suit, card power, legal plays
description:
## Objective
Follow/legality core: effectiveSuit, cardPower, legalPlays with bower and joker semantics exactly matching the oracle.

## Behavioral context
After this leaf the engine can answer, for any hand/trump/led-suit, which cards are legal and which card wins a trick — including left-bower-follows-trump and joker-blocks-sluffing in NT/nulla.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/engine/src/tricks.ts`: port effective_suit (five_hundred.py 142-154), card_power (157-171), legal_plays (174-186) with identical numeric power constants (joker 3000, right bower 2999, left bower 2998, trump 2000+r, led 1000+r, else 0).

## Non-goals
No trick loop or winner bookkeeping (separate leaf); no policy logic.

## Concrete locations
Oracle lines above; SAME_COLOR map (five_hundred.py 49). New file packages/engine/src/tricks.ts. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Keep the exact power-constant scheme so trick winners are comparable to Python outputs during parity replay; trump parameter is `number | null` where null covers NT, nulla, and double nulla (mirrors trump_of).

## Compatibility constraints
Pure functions, no deps; signatures stable for bots and Hard-bot rollouts which call them heavily.

## Ordered steps
1. Port effectiveSuit including joker-is-every-suit (returns ledSuit when trump is null).
2. Port cardPower with bower ordering.
3. Port legalPlays (followers if any, else whole hand).
4. Vitest: port the bower/joker asserts from _self_test (five_hundred.py 654-672) plus left-bower-following and sluff-allowed-in-trump cases.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the cards/ladder leaf. Consumers: auction-less trick play leaf, bots (Easy/Medium/Hard), server validation via legalActions.

## Edge cases
Joker in trump hands counts as trump (can be sluffed onto only per trump rules); holding joker + void in led suit under NT forces the joker (legalPlays = [JOKER]); leading (ledSuit null) returns the whole hand; left bower power beats plain trump ace.

## Plan-gap guidance
If any oracle behavior seems to contradict 500-house-rules.md section "The joker & following suit", record `PLAN-GAP` quoting both; the Python code is the tiebreaker per PRD section 3 but a real conflict must be surfaced, not silently chosen.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: With hearts trump: power(JOKER) > power(JH) > power(JD) > power(AH), and effectiveSuit(JD, trump=H) = H.
- AC-2: Hand [JOKER, 9C] with spades led: legalPlays under NT = [JOKER]; under hearts trump = both cards.
- AC-3: Followers-else-anything holds for ordinary hands (property test over random hands vs a brute-force reference).

title: Engine: cards, deck, bids, and ladder module
description:
## Objective
TS module for card encoding, the 45-card deck, Bid values, and the full bid ladder with nulla/double-nulla placements.

## Behavioral context
Nothing exists in packages/engine yet. After this leaf, all card/bid primitives used by every other engine module exist and match the Python oracle exactly.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Port to `packages/engine/src/cards.ts` and `packages/engine/src/bids.ts`: card encoding helpers, DECK, Bid type, avondale values, bidValue, buildLadder + LADDER + ladderIndex, trumpOf, isLoseAll, cardName for debugging.

## Non-goals
No legality/power logic (separate leaf), no RNG, no state machine.

## Concrete locations
Oracle symbols in five_hundred.py: SUITS/NT/RANKS/JOKER/SAME_COLOR constants (lines 44-50), make_card/card_suit/card_rank/card_name (53-69), DECK (72), Bid dataclass (80-91), _avondale/bid_value (94-105), _build_ladder/LADDER/LADDER_INDEX (108-125), trump_of (128-132), is_lose_all (135-136). Grep/Read fallback used; CodeGraph has no index here.

## Resolved decisions
TS uses the identical integer card encoding `suit*11 + (rank-4)` with JOKER = 44 and suits 0=S,1=C,2=D,3=H, NT strain = 4 — the parity mapping to Python is the identity, which is the simplest bijection allowed by PRD section 3.1. Bid is a plain readonly object `{kind, level, strain}` with kind in NUM|NULLA|DNULLA|IND|PASS; ladder index lookup keys on `kind:level:strain` strings since JS lacks value-equal tuples.

## Compatibility constraints
Zero runtime dependencies in packages/engine (PRD section 2); all types exported for protocol/bots/server reuse.

## Ordered steps
1. Port constants and card helpers to cards.ts.
2. Port Bid, avondale, bidValue, buildLadder, ladderIndex, trumpOf, isLoseAll to bids.ts.
3. Export everything from packages/engine/src/index.ts.
4. Write Vitest cases mirroring the ladder/avondale asserts in _self_test (five_hundred.py lines 661-667).

## Dependencies
Blocked by the M0 scaffold leaf. Consumers: every other engine module, bots, protocol view types.

## Edge cases
Ladder order must place NULLA directly after 7NT and DNULLA between 10D and 10H (rules doc "Bid ranking" section); bidValue of IND and PASS is 0; cardSuit/cardRank of the joker return null.

## Plan-gap guidance
If the rules doc and five_hundred.py ever disagree on ladder placement or avondale values, record `PLAN-GAP` quoting both sources and stop; the planner must arbitrate, not the worker (PRD says Python resolves ambiguity, but a hard conflict is material).

title: Scaffold pnpm monorepo: engine/bots/protocol/server/client packages
description:
## Objective
A one-command pnpm monorepo skeleton with all five workspace packages wired, lint/test/dev scripts working on placeholder code.

## Behavioral context
Today the repo contains only five_hundred.py, 500-house-rules.md, and docs — no JS tooling. After this leaf, `pnpm install`, `pnpm test` (Vitest in every package), and `pnpm dev` (server on port 8500 + Vite client) all succeed.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Root package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, tsconfig.base.json (strict), ESLint + Prettier config; create packages/engine, packages/bots, packages/protocol, apps/server, apps/client each with package.json, src/index.ts, and one trivial Vitest test; wire workspace deps (bots -> engine; server -> engine+bots+protocol; client -> protocol); root scripts: dev, test, build, start; server placeholder must serve GET /healthz on port 8500.

## Non-goals
No game logic, no CI configuration, no deployment tooling, no changes to five_hundred.py or the rules doc.

## Concrete locations
All new files: `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.base.json`, `packages/{engine,bots,protocol}/{package.json,src/index.ts,src/index.test.ts}`, `apps/server/src/index.ts`, `apps/client/` (Vite react-ts template). Grep/Read fallback: verified none of these paths exist yet (repo root listed; greenfield).

## Resolved decisions
pnpm workspaces; TypeScript strict mode; Vitest for all tests; Vite + React for the client; package scope `@five-hundred/*`; Node >= 20; dev server runner is tsx watch; `pnpm dev` uses concurrently to run server + client; prod: `pnpm build` then `pnpm start` serves the built client from the Node server; app name "Five Hundred"; server port 8500 via `PORT` env with 8500 default (PRD section 10 defaults adopted).

## Compatibility constraints
Linux and macOS dev machines; Node >= 20; keep the Python oracle files untouched and excluded from any TS build globs.

## Ordered steps
1. Write root package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, tsconfig.base.json, lint configs.
2. Create the three packages/ libraries with placeholder exports and one test each.
3. Create apps/server with a minimal http server exposing /healthz on PORT (default 8500).
4. Scaffold apps/client from the Vite react-ts template; retitle to "Five Hundred".
5. Wire workspace: dependencies with `workspace:*` and root scripts dev/test/build/start.
6. Run `pnpm install`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm dev` and fix until green; commit pnpm-lock.yaml.

## Dependencies
No issue dependency — first executable leaf. Every later leaf assumes this layout and the `@five-hundred/*` package names.

## Edge cases
`pnpm -r test` must fail loudly (not skip) if a package has no test file — give each package one trivial test; `pnpm dev` must not fail when port 8500 is occupied (print a clear error); lockfile must be committed so installs are reproducible.

## Plan-gap guidance
If npm registry access is unavailable in the working environment, record `PLAN-GAP` with the failing install output and stop; do not vendor node_modules or swap package managers.
acceptance_criteria:

description:
## Objective
The M7 exit gate: in headless simulation, Hard-vs-Medium partnerships win >= 60% of 200+ games, asserted in a repeatable test, with tuning constants finalized.

## Behavioral context
After this leaf the three difficulties provably order Hard > Medium > Easy (Medium > Easy gated in M3), closing the bot strength story (PRD sections 4.3, 7.3).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/bots/test/hardStrength.spec.ts`: simulateGames(200+, [Hard, Medium, Hard, Medium], fixed seed) via the sync headless path with a reduced-but-documented world budget for test runtime; assert wins >= 60%; a `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots sim:hard` CLI for full-budget tuning runs; final tuning of the safety margin / world floors recorded as constants with the sweep summary in a comment.

## Non-goals
No new algorithms — only constant tuning within the sibling-leaf designs; no CI wiring (project has none by scope).

## Concrete locations
Sim harness from M3; HardPolicy sync path from the play leaf. PRD 4.3 acceptance + 8 M7. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
The in-suite run may use a smaller world budget only if the gate still passes at it (documented); if only the full budget passes, the suite marks the full run behind an env flag with the fast run as a >= 55% smoke and the gate documented as the flagged run — transparency over silent weakening (still requires the true gate green before closing).

## Compatibility constraints
Deterministic seeds; runtime of the default test suite kept reasonable (minutes, not hours).

## Ordered steps
1. Wire Hard into the sim harness seat config.
2. Run the 200-game gate at full budget; record the rate.
3. Tune margin/world constants if under 60%; re-run; record the sweep.
4. Land the spec (fast smoke + gated full run per the decision) and the CLI.

## Dependencies
Blocked by: rollout keeps, rollout bidding, rollout play leaves, and the M3 sim harness. Consumers: epic M7 closes here.

## Edge cases
Win-rate variance at n=200 (~3.5% sd around 60%) — if the measured rate is within noise of the gate, run 500 games for the record; seat-position asymmetry (Hard pair as side 0 vs side 1 both measured).

## Plan-gap guidance
If tuning within the designed algorithm cannot reach 60% (fallback budget 2s included), record `PLAN-GAP` with the sweep table — algorithmic redesign is a planning decision (PRD section 9 names the strength test as the gate).

## Observable criteria
- AC-1: The Hard partnership (seats 0 and 2) beats the Medium partnership in >= 60% of >= 200 seeded games at the documented budget.
- AC-2: The result is reproducible from the committed seed and constants via the CLI.
- AC-3: Both side assignments (Hard as side 0 and side 1) meet the gate.

- AC-1: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test -- hardStrength`.
- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots sim:hard -- --games 200 --seed 7`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test -- hardStrength`.

title: Hard bot: rollout card play, time budget, worker-thread pool
description:
## Objective
choosePlay by rollout (each legal card over M sampled worlds with Medium continuations), an enforced per-decision wall-clock budget of about 1s, and a worker_threads pool so Hard never blocks the server event loop.

## Behavioral context
After this leaf Hard is complete and pluggable into the server bot driver via its async decide seam, with the pacing/thinking indicator behavior intact (PRD sections 4.3, 2 bots-in-server bullets).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/bots/src/hard/play.ts`: for each legal card, clone the world, apply, play out with Medium for all seats, average points; adaptive M via a deadline (start coarse, add worlds until deadline; floor 20 worlds or fall back to Medium choice if even that misses the budget — logged); `packages/bots/src/hard/policy.ts`: assemble HardPolicy from keeps/bidding/play leaves (sync API for headless). `apps/server/src/workers/hardPool.ts`: worker pool (size = max(1, cpus-1) capped at 4) receiving {serialized state, seat, seed}, running HardPolicy synchronously in the worker, returning the action; the bot driver decide seam routes Hard seats here; headless sim keeps the sync path (no workers) per PRD 4.4.

## Non-goals
No GPU/wasm optimization; no cross-decision caching; no UI (the thinking indicator is client work in M8, driven by existing actingSeat data).

## Concrete locations
Bot driver seam from the M4 bot-driver leaf (`decide(seat, state)`); engine serialization from the assembly leaf (worker transfer); sibling leaves for decisions. Oracle anchor for budget expectations: PRD 4.3 (~50-200 worlds, 0.5-2s fallback acceptance). Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Deadline default 1000ms (env-tunable HARD_BOT_BUDGET_MS; risk fallback per PRD section 9 allows up to 2s); worker pool is server-side only — packages/bots stays worker-free so the client never bundles worker code; state crosses the worker boundary via the engine JSON serialization; per-decision seed = game seed + action count for reproducibility.

## Compatibility constraints
Node worker_threads only (no browser workers needed — Hard runs server-side); headless sim path must remain synchronous and budget-free for tests that need determinism over speed.

## Ordered steps
1. Rollout choosePlay with deadline-adaptive M and Medium fallback.
2. HardPolicy assembly implementing the full Policy interface.
3. Server worker pool + decide-seam routing for Hard seats.
4. Tests: budget respected (wall-clock assertion with slack); event loop unblocked during a Hard decision (concurrent ping test on the server); worker crash recovery (pool respawns, decision retried once, then Medium fallback with error log).
5. Headless bench: worlds/decision achieved on the dev box recorded in notes on close.

## Dependencies
Blocked by: world sampler, rollout keeps, rollout bidding leaves, and the M4 bot-driver leaf (seam). Related: bot pacing (delay + thinking states). Consumers: strength gate; production play.

## Edge cases
One-legal-card turns skip rollouts entirely (instant); late tricks with tiny hidden sets converge fast (cap M at what the deadline allows, no busywait); simultaneous Hard decisions in multiple rooms queue on the pool without starvation (FIFO); room deletion mid-decision discards the result.

## Plan-gap guidance
If the 60% strength gate later fails specifically due to budget starvation (worlds too few at 1s), the documented fallback is raising toward 2s per PRD section 9 — apply it; anything beyond 2s or algorithmic redesign is a `PLAN-GAP`.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: Hard decisions complete within the configured budget (+100ms slack) across a seeded 50-decision run.
- AC-2: The server answers a concurrent healthz/ping while a Hard decision is in flight (event loop never blocked).
- AC-3: A killed worker mid-decision recovers: pool respawns and the game continues without a stuck room.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test -- hardplay`.
- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/server test -- hardpool`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/server test -- hardpool`.

## Targeted tests
Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test -- test/hardPlay.spec.ts` and `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/server test -- test/hardPool.spec.ts` (specs added by this leaf).

title: Hard bot: rollout bidding including nulla/dnulla/slam
description:
## Objective
chooseBid and considerSlam for Hard: estimate make-probability of candidate contracts by rollout and bid up the ladder while EV(bid) exceeds EV(pass) with a safety margin; slam/nulla/dnulla likewise evaluated by rollout.

## Behavioral context
After this leaf Hard bids to its cards rather than heuristics — the second pillar of its strength edge (PRD section 4.3 bidding).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/bots/src/hard/bidding.ts`: candidate contracts = each strain at the minimum currently-available level (plus one level up when strong), nulla when the hand is low, dnulla only over a partner nulla-suggestive context is out of scope (no signaling model) — dnulla candidates gated on own-hand lowness; for each candidate: sample worlds, simulate exchange (Hard keeps via a cheap Medium-keeps proxy to bound cost) + play-out with Medium policies, EV in expected points including set risk; bid the best candidate whose EV beats pass-EV by the margin; considerSlam: rollout the slam variant vs non-slam on the actual 15, threshold on EV difference; indications: indicate best suit when below bidding strength but est is decent (reuse the Medium indication rule verbatim — decision).

## Non-goals
No partner-signal inference from indications (v1 simplification, recorded); no opponent bid inference constraints on worlds during the auction.

## Concrete locations
Ladder/EV primitives from packages/engine; world sampler + play-out helpers from sibling leaves; Medium policy as rollout opponent; oracle anchor: RandomPolicy/HeuristicPolicy bid shapes (five_hundred.py 225-231, 278-298) inform candidate pruning. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Pass-EV counts the expected defender points + the risk of opponents making their likely contract at a coarse estimate (single-world cheap heuristic, not full opponent rollout — bounded cost); safety margin default +25 expected points (tunable constant, tuned at the strength gate); world count per candidate adaptive within the 1s budget shared with the integration leaf; auction worlds ignore prior bids as constraints (documented simplification per Non-goals).

## Compatibility constraints
Pure/synchronous; every returned bid must be in the current legal set (validated in tests against engine legalBids).

## Ordered steps
1. Candidate generation from ladder position + hand shape gates.
2. Rollout EV evaluator per candidate (shared worlds).
3. Pass-EV baseline + margin comparison; bid selection.
4. considerSlam rollout on the 15.
5. Tests: strong trump fixture bids that suit; garbage hand passes; uniformly-low no-joker hand finds nulla; slam fires on a near-certain fixture and not on a marginal one; all outputs legal.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the world sampler leaf. Related: rollout keeps leaf (shares play-out helpers). Consumers: strength gate leaf.

## Edge cases
Ladder top (only pass legal); being outbid repeatedly must not loop (each call independent); dnulla EV must include the partner pass-through unknown (worlds cover it); indication legality one-per-auction respected via may-indicate input.

## Plan-gap guidance
The PRD demands EV-driven ladder climbing but gives no margin value — the +25 default is a planning decision recorded here and tuned only via the strength gate; if the gate cannot be met at any margin, record `PLAN-GAP` with the tuning sweep results.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: Fixture hands produce sensible contracts: strong-hearts bids hearts; garbage passes; low-no-joker finds nulla; near-certain slam declares.
- AC-2: Every bid/slam decision over 1000 seeded auction contexts is legal per engine legalBids.
- AC-3: Decisions are deterministic under a fixed seed.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test -- bidding`.
- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test -- bidding`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test -- bidding`.

## Targeted tests
Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test -- test/bidding.spec.ts` (spec added by this leaf under `packages/bots/test/`).

title: Hard bot: rollout keep/discard evaluation
description:
## Objective
chooseKeeps for Hard: generate candidate keep-sets heuristically, evaluate each over N sampled worlds with Medium play-outs, pick the best — a port and extension of evaluate_keeps.

## Behavioral context
After this leaf Hard makes materially better exchange decisions than Medium, the highest-leverage decision in the game (it sees 15 of 45 cards).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/bots/src/hard/keeps.ts`: candidate generation = Medium chooseKeeps result + systematic variations (swap each kept marginal card with each discarded near-marginal card, cap ~12 candidates; include the lose-all weakest-10 candidate on nulla/dnulla); evaluation = for each candidate, over N worlds: deal hidden seats (world sampler), play out with Medium policies for everyone (port _play_fixed generalized to all contract classes incl. lose-all and slam-16 contexts), success metric = made? for the contract (or expected points — decision below); pick argmax.

## Non-goals
No slam decision here (bidding leaf owns considerSlam); no worker threading (integration leaf); no candidate search beyond the swap neighborhood.

## Concrete locations
Oracle: evaluate_keeps (five_hundred.py 597-615) and _play_fixed (618-646, numbered-bids-only — must be generalized); Medium policy from its leaf; world sampler sibling. New file above. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Metric is expected declarer-side points delta, not raw make-rate (captures defender-point leakage and slam stakes; make-rate alone is the oracle simplification); N adaptive to the time budget with a floor of 30 worlds per candidate (tuned in the integration leaf); shared world reuse across candidates (same sampled worlds evaluate every candidate — variance reduction and cache friendliness).

## Compatibility constraints
Pure/synchronous given (state, rng) so the worker leaf can wrap it; must respect the Policy interface signature.

## Ordered steps
1. Generalize a fixed-hand play-out helper for all contract classes (reuses engine play loop).
2. Candidate generator with the swap neighborhood + lose-all candidate.
3. Shared-worlds evaluator with expected-points metric.
4. Tests: on a constructed obviously-strong-keep fixture Hard picks the dominant keep; on a nulla fixture picks weakest-10; evaluator determinism under fixed rng.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the world sampler leaf. Consumers: strength gate leaf; worker integration wraps this.

## Edge cases
Slam context evaluates 16-keep-10; dnulla declarer keeps must also consider what the 5 discards do to the PARTNER (evaluate the pass-through by letting Medium partner-keeps run inside the play-out); candidate ties broken by first-in-order for determinism.

## Plan-gap guidance
If expected-points vs make-rate materially disagree on ordering and the strength gate fails either way, record `PLAN-GAP` with both measurements rather than metric-shopping.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: On constructed fixtures Hard chooseKeeps beats Medium chooseKeeps in evaluated expected points (self-consistency check).
- AC-2: Nulla and slam-16 contexts produce valid 10-card keeps with the correct special-case behavior.
- AC-3: Identical (state, seed) inputs always produce identical keeps.

title: Hard bot: constrained world sampler
description:
## Objective
Determinization core: sample complete deals of the unseen cards to hidden seats, uniformly at random but consistent with observed constraints (revealed voids, known sat-out hands, cards already played).

## Behavioral context
No hidden-information machinery exists. After this leaf the Hard bot leaves can roll out any decision point over sampled worlds (PRD section 4.3 world sampling).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/bots/src/hard/worlds.ts`: ObservedConstraints derived from a seat-local game view/history {my cards, played cards, middle knowledge if I exchanged, per-seat void suits observed when a player failed to follow, hand sizes}; sampleWorld(constraints, rng) -> full hands for hidden seats; rejection sampling with a constructive fallback (deal suits respecting voids first) so pathological constraint sets terminate; extraction of constraints from the engine state/trick history.

## Non-goals
No rollout/EV logic (sibling leaves); no inference beyond hard constraints (no probabilistic opponent modeling).

## Concrete locations
Extends the approach of evaluate_keeps unseen-card dealing (five_hundred.py 597-615: unseen = DECK minus my15, shuffle, slice to other seats) with the play-phase void constraints PRD 4.3 requires; uses engine trick history from the assembly leaf; new files under packages/bots/src/hard/. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Voids are detected from effective-suit failure to follow (a player not following the led effective suit is void in it — mirrors legal_plays semantics); constructive fallback: assign void-restricted seats last from suit-partitioned pools, retry cap 1000 then throw (a throw is a bug signal, not a fallback); sampler is pure given (constraints, rng) for testability.

## Compatibility constraints
Must run identically in worker threads and main thread; no engine mutation — worlds are fresh state fragments.

## Ordered steps
1. Constraint extraction from state + trick history (unit-tested against constructed histories).
2. Uniform sampler with rejection + constructive fallback.
3. Statistical tests: over many samples, all worlds satisfy constraints; unconstrained sampling is card-uniform within tolerance; a known-void seat never receives that suit.
4. Bench note: samples/sec recorded for budget tuning (informational).

## Dependencies
Blocked by the sim harness leaf (drives play-outs used in validation). Consumers: the three rollout leaves.

## Edge cases
Late-hand states where few cards are hidden (sampler must handle 1-2 unknown cards); sat-out seats hold no hand (nulla/slam) — excluded from dealing; the dnulla partner knows 5 passed cards (constraint: those are NOT in hidden seats); exchange-phase declarer knows all 15 (middle absorbed).

## Plan-gap guidance
If the redacted view lacks data the constraint extractor needs (e.g. per-trick effective led suit), extend via the engine trick history rather than re-deriving; if that requires new engine state, record `PLAN-GAP` against the assembly leaf.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: 10k sampled worlds from a mid-play fixture all satisfy every void/hand-size/played-card constraint.
- AC-2: Unconstrained early-auction sampling distributes each unseen card across hidden seats uniformly within statistical tolerance.
- AC-3: Constraint extraction from a constructed trick history detects exactly the planted voids.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test -- worlds`.
- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test -- worlds`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test -- worlds`.

## Targeted tests
Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test -- test/worlds.spec.ts` (spec added by this leaf under `packages/bots/test/`).

title: Client: joker UX — lead suit picker and sluff-block explanation

description:
## Objective
The complete slam UX: offer + confirm on the exchange screen with the exact stake wording, the partner best-card surrender picker with a suggested strongest card, and clear sitting-out presentation afterward.

## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Slam offer panel beside the ExchangePicker on numbered contracts: text "Declare slam — play alone for all 10 tricks: +{value+250} or -{value+250}" with confirm/decline two-step; on slam: declarer waits for partner card, then the picker runs in 16-keep-10 mode (maxKeep prop from the M5 picker); partner-side `GiveCardPicker` — pick 1 card with the UI pre-suggesting the strongest (via pure cardPower helper) but free choice; sat-out ribbon + "sitting out (slam)" state on the partner seat for all players.

## Non-goals
No slam advice/EV hints; no changes to bot slam logic.

## Concrete locations
Extends ExchangePicker mount in Table.tsx; new GiveCardPicker component; declareSlam/declineSlam/giveCard commands; stake values from bidValue helper. PRD 6.2 wording. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Decline is explicit (declineSlam) so the offer never silently lapses; the suggestion uses max cardPower with the contract trump (mirrors the Python give_best_card default, five_hundred.py 205-208) but the human can pick any card; the surrendered card is visible only to the declarer (it is in their 16) — other seats see the abstract "partner gave their best card".

## Compatibility constraints
Confirm step mandatory (a slam is near game-deciding per the rules doc); phone-width layouts.

## Ordered steps
1. Slam offer + confirm with stake interpolation.
2. Wait state + 16-card picker mode for the declarer.
3. GiveCardPicker with suggestion.
4. Sat-out presentation.

Bot partner (giveCard happens server-side instantly — declarer just sees the 16); human declarer declines then proceeds normally; reconnect during each sub-state restores the right panel; slam by a bot declarer with a human partner (partner gets the picker).

## Objective
Hand-end overlay (contract result, per-side deltas, running totals, next-hand ready-up) and game-end screen (winner, final score, rematch with same seats/bots).

## Readiness schema
v1

`apps/client/src/components/HandEndOverlay.tsx` (made/set headline, contract, deltas per side incl. defender points, running totals, "Ready" button sending nextHand, per-seat readiness ticks); `apps/client/src/screens/GameEnd.tsx` (winner, final scores, out-the-back callout when the loser crossed -500, rematch button host-only sending a rematch command); protocol/server addition: rematch command resetting scores and starting a fresh game with the same seats/bots (small server change owned here, validated same as startGame).

New files above; handScored/gameOver events from protocol; server rematch handling added beside startGame in apps/server/src/rooms.ts. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

Ready-up shows who is not ready yet (names), bots always ready; rematch is host-only and yields a fresh seed; the overlay also announces slam/nulla results in words (e.g. "Slam failed: -550") so scoring is explainable to family players.

## Compatibility constraints
Overlay must not block viewing the final trick beneath it (translucent scrim, dismissible to peek, ready state preserved).

Blocked by the card-play leaf (loop must reach handScored). Consumers: M8 Playwright drives these; epic M5 closes here.

The rematch command is a protocol addition sanctioned by PRD 6.1 ("rematch (same room, same seats/bots)"); anything beyond reset-and-restart (e.g. carrying dealer rotation across games) is undecided — record `PLAN-GAP` if it matters to acceptance.

title: Client: WS connection, state store, seq gap recovery
description:
## Objective
The client data layer: a WebSocket client with typed send/receive, a state store holding roomState + gameView, seq gap detection with requestState recovery, and localStorage token persistence.

## Behavioral context
The scaffolded client renders a placeholder. After this leaf any screen can subscribe to live room/game state, and a dropped or gappy connection self-heals (PRD sections 5, 6).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`apps/client/src/net/socket.ts` (connect, auto-reconnect with backoff, typed send via protocol guards); `apps/client/src/store.ts` (React context + useSyncExternalStore or zustand — decision below; holds roomView, seatView, lastError, connection status); seq handling: ignore stale, apply monotonic, on gap send requestState; persist {roomCode, seatToken, name} in localStorage and auto-rejoin on load.

## Non-goals
No screen components; no styling; no game rendering.

## Concrete locations
New `apps/client/src/net/socket.ts` (functions `connect()` and typed `send()`, auto-reconnect with backoff) and `apps/client/src/store.ts` (`createStore()` / `applyServerEvent()`; holds roomView, seatView, lastError, connection status); message and view types imported from `packages/protocol/src/messages.ts` via @five-hundred/protocol; dev server URL from Vite env (ws://localhost:8500 in dev, same-origin in prod). Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
State store is zustand (tiny, no boilerplate, works outside React for socket callbacks) — the single allowed client state dep; ws URL derives from location with a VITE_SERVER_URL dev override; auto-rejoin runs only when localStorage holds a token and the server confirms (badToken clears storage).

## Compatibility constraints
Works in evergreen desktop + mobile browsers; no Node-only APIs; reconnect backoff caps at 5s so battery is respected.

## Ordered steps
1. Implement socket wrapper with connect/reconnect/backoff and typed dispatch.
2. Implement the store with actions mirroring server events.
3. Implement seq monotonic/gap logic + requestState.
4. Implement localStorage persistence and auto-rejoin flow.
5. Vitest (jsdom + mock ws server via vitest-websocket-mock or a hand-rolled mock): gap triggers requestState; stale seq dropped; token auto-rejoin happy/badToken paths.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the protocol leaf and the server game-loop leaf (a live server to develop against). Consumers: every client screen leaf.

## Edge cases
Server restart mid-session (rejoin gets badRoomCode -> clear and return home); out-of-order events after reconnect (full view resets the baseline seq); double-tab on the same token (server latest-attach-wins; the losing tab shows a clear "seat opened elsewhere" state).

## Plan-gap guidance
If protocol events prove insufficient to rebuild UI state after reconnect (missing fields in views), record `PLAN-GAP` against the protocol leaf; do not cache hidden information client-side to compensate.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: A simulated event stream with a seq gap triggers exactly one requestState and converges to the full view.
- AC-2: Reload with a stored valid token rejoins the same seat automatically; with an invalid token, storage is cleared and the home flow shown.
- AC-3: Stale (lower-seq) events never overwrite newer state.

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/client test -- store`.
- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/client test -- store`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/client test -- store`.

## Targeted tests
Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/client test -- src/net/socket.test.ts src/store.test.ts` (specs added by this leaf; cover reconnect/backoff, seq gap recovery, and localStorage rejoin).

## Scope
Extend joinRoom handling in rooms.ts/game.ts: joinRoom {code, token} reattaches the socket to the seat and replies with roomState + full gameView at current seq; mark seats connected/disconnected on socket close; while the acting seat is a disconnected human, the game simply waits (bots never act for them in v1) and all clients see a paused indicator flag on roomState; host command convertSeatToBot {seat, difficulty} allowed only while that seat is disconnected and a game is running.

## Non-goals
No bot-takeover-on-timeout automation; no multi-device same-seat support (new token invalidates nothing — one socket per seat, latest attach wins).

## Concrete locations
rooms.ts (join/attach, connection flags), game.ts (paused flag in broadcasts), protocol additions: convertSeatToBot command + seat-connection fields on RoomView (extend the protocol leaf types here). PRD section 5 bullet 2. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Latest-attach-wins for duplicate tokens (old socket closed with a typed error) — simplest recovery from zombie tabs; pause is purely implicit (server just waits) plus a boolean so UIs can show it; convertSeatToBot is irreversible for the rest of the game (v1; the human token is invalidated).

## Compatibility constraints
Token in localStorage per PRD; reconnect must work mid-auction, mid-exchange, and mid-trick (full view resend covers all phases).

## Ordered steps
1. Implement token reattach on joinRoom with full-state resend.
2. Track connected state per seat; broadcast on change.
3. Implement convertSeatToBot with validation (host, disconnected seat, game running) and bot-driver handoff.
4. Vitest with real ws: drop a socket mid-trick, reattach with token, assert identical view; convert a dropped seat to a bot and play on.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the game-loop leaf and the bot driver leaf (handoff). Consumers: client store reconnect logic; integration tests.

## Edge cases
Reattach with a wrong token -> badToken; reattach after the room was GC-swept -> badRoomCode; disconnect during the pacing delay of a bot (no pause — only human turns pause); host disconnects mid-game (host powers follow the token, so a reconnected host resumes them; no transfer mid-game in v1); convertSeatToBot on the host seat itself rejected.

## Plan-gap guidance
Mid-game host succession when the host never returns is undecided in the PRD — the seat can be converted only BY the host, so a vanished host can stall a game; this is accepted v1 behavior. If a stakeholder requires otherwise, that is a `PLAN-GAP` for planning, not an implementer choice.

- AC-2: While the acting human is disconnected the game makes no progress, and roomState shows the paused/disconnected flags.
- AC-3: convertSeatToBot on a disconnected seat hands the seat to a bot which then acts; the old token is rejected thereafter.

title: Server: bot turn driver with pacing delay
description:
## Objective
Whenever the acting seat is a bot, the server invokes its policy and applies the result after a randomized human-pacing delay.

## Behavioral context
After this leaf 1 human + 3 bots (Easy/Medium) is fully playable end to end on the server; Hard bots plug into the same driver later via the worker pool.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`apps/server/src/botDriver.ts`: after every state advance, if the acting seat is a bot, schedule policy invocation; map engine phase to the right Policy method (chooseBid, chooseKeeps, considerSlam, giveBestCard, choosePlay incl. joker suit choice); apply via the same validated path as human commands; pacing delay uniform 500-1500ms (config constant), 0 in test mode.

## Non-goals
No Hard bot / worker threads (M7 wires into the hook left here); no UI thinking indicator (client leaf).

## Concrete locations
Builds on game.ts apply path; policies from @five-hundred/bots (Easy/Medium per seat difficulty stored in Room). PRD sections 4.4 (pacing) and 5 (game loop bullet). Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Bot decisions run on the event loop for E/M (they are microsecond-fast); the driver exposes an async `decide(seat, state)` seam so M7 can swap in a worker-pool implementation for Hard without touching the loop; per-bot Rng seeded from the game seed + seat for reproducibility; delays via setTimeout with a test-mode zero override; chained bot turns (bot after bot) each get their own delay.

## Compatibility constraints
Bot actions must pass the same validation as humans (never bypass); the event loop must never block (E/M only here).

## Ordered steps
1. Implement seat-difficulty -> Policy instance resolution on game start.
2. Implement the after-advance hook detecting bot turns incl. multi-action phases (slam decide then keeps).
3. Implement pacing with test-mode override.
4. Vitest: 1 stub human + 3 bots play a full hand to handScored with delays zeroed; a full game to gameOver.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the game-loop leaf and the Medium bot leaf. Consumers: M7 worker-pool leaf replaces the decide seam for Hard seats; integration tests run full bot games.

## Edge cases
Bot must auto-ready nextHand; bot as slam partner must giveCard; bot declarer on dnulla triggers partner pass-through automatically; room deleted (GC/all humans left) mid-delay must cancel pending timers; a bot action rejected by validation is a hard bug — crash the room with a logged error rather than looping.

## Plan-gap guidance
If any phase leaves a bot with no matching Policy method (interface gap vs the engine action set), record `PLAN-GAP` naming the phase; do not improvise a default action.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: 1 scripted human + 3 bots complete a full game to gameOver in test mode with zero validation rejections.
- AC-2: In non-test mode, consecutive bot actions are spaced by at least 500ms (timer inspection with fake timers).
- AC-3: Killing the room cancels all pending bot timers (no post-deletion sends).

## Criterion checks

- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/server test -- botDriver`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/server test -- botDriver`.

title: Server: authoritative game loop with validation and redacted broadcasts
description:
## Objective
The server-side game driver: startGame creates a seeded engine GameState; every game command is validated against legalActions for the sending seat; per-seat redacted views broadcast with seq; typed rejections change nothing.

## Behavioral context
After this leaf humans in a room actually play: bids, discards, plays flow through the engine, and every client only ever sees its own cards (PRD sections 5 Validation and Game loop).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`apps/server/src/game.ts`: map protocol commands (bid, discardKeeps, declareSlam, declineSlam, giveCard, playCard, nextHand, requestState) to engine actions; validate sender token -> seat -> engine legality; on success applyAction, bump seq, send each seat its redactedView (gameView) plus actionRequest to the acting seat; emit trickResolved, handScored, gameOver events at the corresponding transitions; on failure send typed error to the sender only.

## Non-goals
No bot turns (next leaf); no reconnect (later leaf); no pacing.

## Concrete locations
Builds on rooms.ts startGame hook; engine API applyAction/legalActions/redactedView from packages/engine/src/state.ts; protocol events from packages/protocol. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Game seed = crypto random 32-bit int recorded on the Room for debugging; nextHand requires every human seat to send it (ready-up per PRD section 6.1 hand-end overlay) — bot seats auto-ready; trickResolved is emitted with the completed trick and winner before the next gameView so the client can linger on it; requestState resends the full current view with the current seq.

## Compatibility constraints
All hidden-information redaction happens exclusively through engine redactedView — the server never hand-builds views (single redaction path is what the integration tests assert against).

## Ordered steps
1. Implement command -> action mapping with token/seat resolution.
2. Implement validation flow returning protocol error codes (notYourTurn, illegalAction).
3. Implement broadcast: per-seat gameView + actionRequest + phase-transition events.
4. Wire startGame to deal and enter auction; wire hand/game transitions incl. redeal notification.
5. Vitest with real ws clients: a scripted 2-human game segment; illegal command rejection leaves state unchanged (seq does not advance).

## Dependencies
Blocked by the rooms leaf and the engine assembly leaf. Consumers: bot driver invokes the same apply path; client store consumes the events.

## Edge cases
Command from a socket without a seated token; command for a bot-occupied seat; playCard with a stale seq client-side (server ignores client seq — validation is by state, seq is for clients); double-send of the same command (second is illegal, state unchanged); redeal mid-auction must notify all seats.

## Plan-gap guidance
If any engine action requires server-side interpretation beyond 1:1 mapping (a sign the engine API is incomplete), record `PLAN-GAP` naming the command and engine gap; do not implement rules logic in the server.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: A scripted auction + exchange + first trick between 2 ws clients (2 seats pre-filled with engine-driven stub actions) advances state and every client receives strictly increasing seq values.
- AC-2: An illegal command receives a typed error, and the next gameView seq shows no state advance.
- AC-3: No gameView sent to seat A ever contains a card id from another hand, the middle, or discards (message inspection helper).

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/server test -- game`.
- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/server test -- game`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/server test -- redaction`.

## Targeted tests
Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/server test -- test/game.spec.ts` (spec added by this leaf under `apps/server/test/`).
