title: Server: room lifecycle — create/join/sit/configure bots/start, idle GC
description:
## Objective
In-memory room management over WebSockets: room codes, seat claiming, host powers (bot difficulties, start), seat tokens, and 2h-idle garbage collection.

## Behavioral context
After this leaf up to 4 browsers can create/join a room, claim seats, configure bots for empty seats, and the host can start a game (engine wiring lands in the next leaf, so start may stub the game object).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`apps/server/src/rooms.ts`: Room type {code, seats[4] (human token/name or bot difficulty), hostSeat, game or null, seq, lastActivity, sockets}; Map<roomCode, Room>; handlers for createRoom, joinRoom, sit, configureBots, startGame; roomState broadcast on every change; GC sweep. `apps/server/src/ws.ts`: ws server setup on PORT (default 8500), connection/message plumbing, envelope + seq stamping.

## Non-goals
No game-command handling (next leaf); no reconnect semantics beyond token issuance (reconnect leaf); no persistence.

## Concrete locations
New `apps/server/src/rooms.ts` (Room type; handlers `createRoom()`, `joinRoom()`, `sit()`, `configureBots()`, `startGame()`; idle GC sweep) and `apps/server/src/ws.ts` (ws server setup on PORT, connection/message plumbing, envelope + seq stamping); uses the `ws` npm package (server dep added here); protocol types from `packages/protocol/src/messages.ts` (@five-hundred/protocol). PRD section 5 "Rooms" and "Ops" bullets are the spec. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Room codes: 5 chars from A-Z + 2-9 excluding O/I (unambiguous), collision-retried; seat tokens: crypto.randomUUID issued on sit, sent only to that socket; host = first joiner, transfers to the next human if the host leaves pre-game; empty seats at startGame become bots at their configured difficulty (default Medium); GC: sweep every 5 minutes, delete rooms idle >= 2 hours, closing sockets with a typed error.

## Compatibility constraints
Single process, in-memory only (PRD scope); PORT env respected; must serve the built client statically in prod mode (wire the static route here since it is ops plumbing).

## Ordered steps
1. Add ws + static serving to apps/server; envelope send helper with per-room seq.
2. Implement Room store, code generation, createRoom/joinRoom.
3. Implement sit (token issuance), configureBots (host only), startGame (host only; converts empties to bots; stubs game start hook).
4. Implement GC sweep and lastActivity touching.
5. Vitest with real ws clients: create/join/sit/start happy path, seatTaken, notHost, badRoomCode errors.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the protocol leaf. Consumers: game-loop leaf plugs into the startGame hook; reconnect leaf extends joinRoom; client lobby leaf consumes roomState.

## Edge cases
Joining a full room; sitting in an occupied seat; two tabs claiming one seat (second sit rejected); configureBots on an occupied seat rejected; startGame with zero humans rejected (notHost covers non-host; add badCommand for empty rooms); GC firing while a socket is mid-message.

## Plan-gap guidance
PRD leaves host-departure policy unstated pre-game (host transfer decided here) but says nothing about mid-game host leave — the reconnect leaf owns that; if it surfaces here, record `PLAN-GAP` rather than deciding twice.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: Two ws clients can create + join a room, claim seats, and both receive identical roomState with increasing seq.
- AC-2: Host-only actions (configureBots, startGame) are rejected for non-hosts with the notHost error code.
- AC-3: A room idle past the threshold is GC-swept (verified with fake timers).

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/server test -- rooms`.
- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/server test -- rooms`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/server test -- gc`.

## Targeted tests
Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/server test -- test/rooms.spec.ts` (spec added by this leaf under `apps/server/test/`).

title: Protocol package: typed messages, redacted views, sequence numbers
description:
## Objective
The shared client/server contract in packages/protocol: every command, event, error code, and the per-seat view types, with sequence numbering.

## Behavioral context
No contract exists. After this leaf, server and client compile against one set of types and any state-bearing message carries a monotonically increasing seq (PRD section 5).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/protocol/src/messages.ts`: client commands createRoom, joinRoom, sit, configureBots, startGame, bid, discardKeeps, declareSlam (and declineSlam), giveCard, playCard, chooseJokerSuit (folded into playCard per the engine decision — kept as a playCard field), nextHand, plus requestState for gap recovery; server events roomState, gameView, actionRequest, trickResolved, handScored, gameOver, error; `packages/protocol/src/views.ts`: RoomView (seats, names, bot difficulties, host), SeatGameView wrapping the engine redactedView plus seq; error codes enum.

## Non-goals
No transport code, no validation logic (server leaf), no React types.

## Concrete locations
New `packages/protocol/src/messages.ts` (command/event unions, `interface Envelope` carrying seq) and `packages/protocol/src/guards.ts` (type guards `isCommand()` / `isEvent()`, reused by the server integration suite); imports view/state types from `packages/engine/src/state.ts` via @five-hundred/engine. PRD section 5 message list is the source; deviations recorded under Resolved decisions. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
chooseJokerSuit is not a standalone command — the engine models it as a playCard field, so the protocol matches (PRD lists it as a command; folding it is a deliberate simplification recorded here); added requestState (client asks for a full view after a seq gap) and declineSlam (explicit exchange progression); seq is per-room, increments on every state-bearing event, and lives on the envelope `{seq, event}`; all messages are JSON with a `t` discriminant field.

## Compatibility constraints
Types only — the package must have zero runtime code beyond type guards, so client bundle stays lean; JSON-serializable throughout.

## Ordered steps
1. Define command union with per-command payloads and a Zod-free hand-rolled type-guard module (decision: no runtime dep; guards are small).
2. Define event union + envelope with seq.
3. Define RoomView/SeatGameView re-using engine redacted types.
4. Define typed error codes (badCommand, notYourTurn, illegalAction, badRoomCode, seatTaken, notHost, badToken).
5. Unit tests for the type guards on valid/invalid payload samples.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the GameState assembly leaf (view types). Consumers: apps/server handlers, apps/client store, integration tests.

## Edge cases
Unknown message type must be guard-rejected, not crash; forward-compat: envelope tolerates unknown extra fields; seq must be present on roomState and gameView but not required on error.

## Plan-gap guidance
If an engine action proves unrepresentable in the command set while building the server (e.g. a phase needing a command not in PRD section 5), record `PLAN-GAP` naming the phase and candidate command instead of overloading an existing message.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: Server and client packages compile against protocol types with strict TS.
- AC-2: Type guards accept every valid sample and reject malformed samples for each command/event.
- AC-3: The envelope carries seq on all state-bearing events (compile-time enforced).

## Criterion checks
- AC-1: Run `pnpm -r exec tsc --noEmit` (post-integration; initially `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/protocol exec tsc --noEmit`).
- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/protocol test`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/protocol test -- envelope`.

## Targeted tests
Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/protocol test -- src/messages.test.ts` (colocated Vitest spec per the scaffold convention; added by this leaf).

title: Bots: headless sim harness and Medium-beats-Easy gate
description:
## Objective
TS ports of simulate_hands / simulate_games / print_stats plus the strength acceptance test: Medium-vs-Easy partnerships win >= 60% over 200+ games.

## Behavioral context
After this leaf bot strength is measurable and gated, and the same harness later gates the Hard bot (PRD sections 4.4, 7.3).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/bots/src/sim.ts`: simulateHands(n, policies, seed) -> per-contract stats map; simulateGames(n, policies, seed) -> win counts; printStats table equivalent; drives full games through the engine GameState API with no pacing delays. Strength spec `packages/bots/test/strength.spec.ts`: Medium (side 0) vs Easy (side 1), 200 games, assert wins[0]/200 >= 0.6. CLI entry `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots sim` for manual tuning runs.

## Non-goals
No Hard bot; no UI; no parallelism (200 games of E/M bots is fast).

## Concrete locations
Oracle: simulate_hands (five_hundred.py 561-574), print_stats (577-582), simulate_games (585-591), play_game accumulation (537-555) already ported in the engine scoring leaf — the harness drives the public API rather than re-implementing scoring. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Harness lives in packages/bots (not engine) since it depends on policies; stats keyed by contract string + slam marker exactly like the oracle so outputs are comparable; the 200-game gate runs in the normal test suite with a fixed seed (must complete in well under a minute; if slower, profile before reducing scope).

## Compatibility constraints
Headless mode is synchronous and must never sleep (PRD section 4.4: pacing skipped in headless mode).

## Ordered steps
1. Implement the game driver: policies x GameState until gameOver, with redeal handling.
2. Implement simulateHands/simulateGames/printStats.
3. Sanity-compare 5k-hand Medium-only stats against the Python printout shape (made% within a few points — informational, recorded in notes on close).
4. Add the Medium-vs-Easy 200-game gate spec with fixed seed.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the Easy and Medium leaves. Consumers: Hard-bot strength gate reuses this harness; server pacing leaf reuses the driver patterns.

## Edge cases
Redeal storms with 4 timid Easy bidders (oracle caps redeals at 10k — mirror a cap and fail loudly); a 300-hand game cap mirroring play_game max_hands with most-points-wins fallback; mixed-seat policy arrays (each seat independently E/M/H per PRD 4.4).

## Plan-gap guidance
If Medium-vs-Easy lands under 60% with a faithful port, that contradicts PRD section 8 M3 acceptance — record `PLAN-GAP` with the measured rate and the fixture-parity evidence (is the port faithful?) rather than tuning Medium ad hoc.
acceptance_criteria:
## Observable criteria
- AC-1: simulateHands(5000) with 4 Medium bots completes and prints a stats table with sane made% values.
- AC-2: Medium-vs-Easy over 200 seeded games: Medium side wins >= 60% (asserted in the suite).

description:
## Objective
A faithful TS port of HeuristicPolicy: strength-based bidding with nulla detection, void-building keeps, cheapest-winner / lose-all-duck play, slam at est >= 8.0, joker led into the shortest suit.

## Behavioral context
After this leaf the Medium bot plays sensible 500 and is the standard opponent/partner model, also reused as the rollout policy inside the Hard bot.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/bots/src/medium.ts`: port every method of HeuristicPolicy (five_hundred.py 241-371) preserving all numeric constants: _suit_strength weights (joker 1.0, bowers 0.95, trump honors 0.55/0.35, side A 0.75, side K 0.25; NT A 0.9, K 0.5, Q 0.2), _lowness >= 8.6 and max rank <= 11 (no joker) for nulla, max_level = min(10, int(est + 2.5)), indication when est >= 4.5 and best strain is a suit, consider_slam est >= 8.0, void-building choose_keeps with the (length, top-rank) dump order and ace floor, duck-with-biggest-loser lose-all play, cheapest-winner otherwise, joker suit = shortest held suit.

## Non-goals
No tuning or strength improvements — fidelity first (strength gate is the sim-harness leaf); no rollout logic.

## Concrete locations
Oracle lines cited above; note int() truncation semantics for max_level must use Math.trunc. New file packages/bots/src/medium.ts. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Port constant-for-constant with named constants and oracle line references in one header block; ties in max()/min() over cards must resolve like Python (first maximal element in iteration order) — iterate hands in sorted card order to make tie-breaks deterministic and document this.

## Compatibility constraints
Pure/synchronous; deterministic under injected Rng (the only rng use is inherited chooseJokerSuit fallback, which Medium overrides).

## Ordered steps
1. Port _suit_strength and _lowness with tests pinning exact values on fixed hands.
2. Port choose_bid incl. nulla branch and indication branch.
3. Port choose_keeps (lose-all weakest-10 branch; void-building branch with fallback).
4. Port consider_slam, choose_joker_suit, choose_play.
5. Cross-check: for a fixed seed, TS Medium decisions equal Python HeuristicPolicy decisions on 100 recorded decision contexts (mini parity fixture generated alongside the M2 trace tooling).

## Dependencies
Blocked by the Policy/Easy leaf (interface + helpers). Related: Python trace emitter (decision-context fixture). Consumers: sim harness, server bot driver, Hard bot rollouts.

## Edge cases
choose_keeps must always return exactly 10 even when the void-builder finds fewer discards (fallback branch, oracle 332-339); nulla branch only when the nulla ladder index is still above ladder_pos; hands of all one suit; keeps from 16 cards after a slam.

## Plan-gap guidance
If Python iteration-order tie-breaking cannot be reproduced for some method and decisions diverge on the fixture, record `PLAN-GAP` with the differing context instead of accepting near-enough behavior — Medium is the Hard-bot rollout model, so drift compounds.

title: Bots: Policy interface and Easy bot
description:
## Objective
The TS Policy interface mirroring the Python one, plus the Easy bot: RandomPolicy port with the two PRD guardrails and no special bids.

## Behavioral context
No bots exist. After this leaf a table of 4 Easy bots can play complete games headlessly via the engine API, and Easy is deliberately beatable (PRD section 4.1).
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
`packages/bots/src/policy.ts`: interface Policy {chooseBid, chooseKeeps, considerSlam, giveBestCard, chooseJokerSuit, choosePlay} typed against engine types with an injected Rng. `packages/bots/src/easy.ts`: port RandomPolicy (five_hundred.py 218-238; default bid_prob 0.15, indicate_prob 0.05) with guardrails: (a) if the partner is currently winning the trick with the top card so far, do not play a higher card when a legal lower card exists; (b) on lose-all contracts prefer a losing card when one exists; plus never bid NULLA/DNULLA and considerSlam always false. Default giveBestCard/chooseJokerSuit inherit the Python base-class behavior (best card by power; random suit).

## Non-goals
No Medium/Hard logic; no pacing delays (server concern); no sim harness (next leaves).

## Concrete locations
Oracle: Policy base (five_hundred.py 192-215), RandomPolicy (218-238). New files as above; packages/bots depends on @five-hundred/engine (workspace). Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
The Policy interface lives in packages/bots, not the engine — the engine stays policy-free (PRD section 2 gives bots -> engine dependency only); "partner winning with a boss card" is computed as: partner holds the current best play in the trick AND no unseen-to-me analysis — just current-trick comparison via cardPower (keep Easy cheap and dumb); random choices draw only from the injected Rng.

## Compatibility constraints
Policies must be pure/synchronous so they run identically in the server, in headless sim, and inside Hard-bot rollouts as opponent models.

## Ordered steps
1. Define the Policy interface + a helpers module (trick winner so far, current best power).
2. Port RandomPolicy bidding (timid ladder step; indications allowed at 0.05) minus NULLA/DNULLA.
3. Port random keeps and random legal play, then layer guardrails (a) and (b).
4. Tests: never bids nulla/dnulla/slam over 10k seeded decisions; guardrail behaviors on constructed tricks; determinism under a fixed Rng.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the GameState assembly leaf. Consumers: Medium bot (interface), sim harness, server bot driver, Hard bot (uses Easy/Medium as rollout opponents).

## Edge cases
Guardrail (a) must not apply when following suit forces a higher card (legal set may contain only winners); guardrail (b) with only winning cards falls back to uniform random; chooseKeeps must return exactly 10 held cards.

## Plan-gap guidance
PRD section 10 fixes the default: Easy never bids slams/nullas. If a guardrail conflicts with legality (no legal card satisfies it), play uniform-random legal — that is in-scope judgment, not a plan gap; anything requiring new engine API is a `PLAN-GAP`.

- AC-1: 4 Easy bots complete 500 seeded headless hands with zero illegal actions.
- AC-2: Over 10k seeded bid decisions Easy never emits NULLA, DNULLA, or a slam declaration.
- AC-3: Guardrail unit cases pass: partner-boss-card restraint and lose-all ducking.

- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test -- easy`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/bots test -- easy`.

description:
## Objective
The PRD 7.5 smoke test: Playwright drives a real browser through create room -> 1 human + 3 bots -> play a full hand to the scoring overlay via UI interactions only.

design:
## Readiness schema

## Scope
`e2e/smoke.test.ts` + playwright.config.ts at the repo root; the config boots the production-mode server (built client, test-mode env: pacing 0, fixed seed, Easy bots for speed and determinism); script: home -> name -> create -> lobby (3 empty seats default difficulty) -> start -> auction (always click Pass when offered; seeded bots produce a contract — seed chosen so a bot wins the auction and the human just follows) -> play legal cards (click first enabled card each turn) -> reach the hand-end overlay; assert overlay content and no console errors.

## Non-goals
No cross-browser matrix (Chromium only); no visual regression; no multi-human E2E (integration tests cover multi-client).

## Concrete locations
New `e2e/smoke.test.ts` and root `playwright.config.ts` (Playwright default testMatch covers `.test.ts`); root package.json script `pnpm e2e`; requires stable data-testid hooks added across client components (small touch-ups in apps/client). PRD 7.5. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Deterministic seed baked via a TEST_SEED env the server honors in test mode only (small server addition owned here); "click any enabled card" keeps the script rules-agnostic — legality dimming does the thinking, which itself smoke-tests the legality UI; Playwright is a root devDependency, not in the client package.

## Compatibility constraints
Runs headless locally via one command with no external services; keeps under ~2 minutes.

## Ordered steps
1. Add data-testid hooks + TEST_SEED support.
2. Playwright config with production-server boot.
3. Script the flow to hand-end; assert overlay + zero console errors.
4. Wire `pnpm e2e`; document in README.

## Dependencies
Blocked by: the hand/game-end leaf (M5) and the server integration suite leaf (M4, stability baseline). Related: M6 leaves (their UI surfaces appear if the seed hits them — seed chosen to avoid special contracts for smoke stability). Consumers: session close protocol / release checks.

## Edge cases
Seed drift if engine/bot code changes decision order (pin by asserting the expected contract in the test so drift fails loudly and the seed gets re-picked consciously); server port collisions (ephemeral port + baseURL wiring); bot instant play in test mode racing UI updates (Playwright auto-wait on enabled selectors covers it).

## Plan-gap guidance
If the pass-through-auction seed approach proves flaky (human unexpectedly wins the auction), scripting the human exchange is in-scope; anything requiring new prod-visible server behavior beyond TEST_SEED is a `PLAN-GAP`.

A theming pass (CSS custom properties, prefers-color-scheme with a manual toggle persisted in localStorage); layout audit + fixes at 375/768/1280 for Home, Lobby, Table (worst case: 15-card exchange fan + bid grid), overlays, GameEnd; card face sizing/typography floor (rank glyph legible at the smallest hand-card size); abstract hidden-event lines styled consistently.

No redesign; no new components; no animations.

Global styles + component CSS across apps/client/src; the Card SVG (table leaf) gains a compact face variant. PRD 6.3. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

CSS custom properties + data-theme attribute (no CSS-in-JS dep); suit colors meet WCAG AA contrast on both themes (red tuned per theme); the 15-card exchange fan wraps to two rows below 500px.

1. Token/theme layer + toggle.
2. Per-screen audit at the three widths; fix worst offenders (exchange fan, bid grid, HUD wrap).

Landscape phones (short viewport: HUD collapses to one line); very long player names (truncate with title); dark-mode card backs contrast.

title: Client polish: trick linger, last-trick peek, thinking indicator
description:
## Objective
Play-flow polish: completed tricks linger ~1.5s with the winner highlighted before clearing, a "last trick" peek control, basic card-movement transitions, and a thinking indicator while a bot decides.

## Behavioral context
After this leaf trick flow is followable at human pace instead of snapping — the PRD 6.2 trick-flow requirements and the PRD 4.3 thinking indicator.
design:
## Readiness schema
v1

## Scope
Trick linger state machine in the table store slice (freeze the resolved trick display 1500ms with winner highlight before clearing — server already sequences trickResolved before the next view per the M4 decision, so the client buffers the next view during linger); LastTrickPeek button/popover rendering the previous trick from the trick history in the view; CSS-transition card movement (hand -> trick area, trick -> winner) kept subtle per PRD non-goals; thinking indicator on the acting seat badge whenever it is a bot seat (pulse + "thinking..." after 400ms).

## Non-goals
No elaborate animation framework; no sound; no replay of older tricks (only the last one, per PRD).

## Concrete locations
Extends TrickArea/SeatBadge/store from M5 leaves; trick history from the engine state (assembly leaf retains it). PRD 6.2 trick flow bullet. Grep/Read fallback; no CodeGraph index.

## Resolved decisions
Linger buffers views client-side rather than the server delaying broadcasts (keeps the server real-time and reconnect-simple); peek shows seat labels + winner ring; transitions are pure CSS (no animation lib dep).

## Compatibility constraints
Linger must not delay YOUR next legal action if you lead the next trick — controls stay live under the linger overlay; reduced-motion media query disables transitions.

## Ordered steps
1. Linger buffer + winner highlight timing.
2. LastTrickPeek from history.
3. CSS transitions + reduced-motion.
4. Thinking indicator.
5. Component tests with fake timers: linger holds then releases the buffered view; peek renders the prior trick; indicator appears only for bot seats.

## Dependencies
Blocked by the card-play leaf (M5). Related: Hard bot play leaf (longer thinks make the indicator matter). Consumers: E2E smoke observes stable behavior.

## Edge cases
Two tricks resolving fast in test-mode botgames (buffer chains without dropping); reconnect during linger (full view wins immediately); hand ending on the lingering trick (overlay waits for linger completion).

## Plan-gap guidance
None expected; purely presentational. Timing constants are product-tunable freely within 1-2s.

- AC-2: The last-trick peek shows the correct previous trick with its winner.
- AC-3: The thinking indicator shows for acting bot seats and never for humans.

- AC-2: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/client test -- polish`.
- AC-3: Run `pnpm --filter @five-hundred/client test -- polish`.
